The d02m-fresh5 draft differs in ids and wording: limit-delete-links (was limit-delete-link); keep-health and keep-signup (were health-keep and signup-keep); keep-redirect is already in the draft, so its earlier re-add is a replace; q-bucket wording changed; q-anon is new and answered auth-only; window-type is not asked, and the fixed window is already in every window item's policy (anchor first_match, boundary exclusive). Each edit names the draft item it acts on by id; draft_mapping maps each drafted id to the decision it follows. Nothing here is a verdict: the edits state the order rules and the gate checks them.

choice_rules.option_label_match: (?i)^(Single 10 per 60s budget shared across all link routes|Shared across GET, POST and DELETE link routes)$
choice_rules.reason: The order says each signed-in user gets ten requests per 60 seconds on the link API, one budget for the API, not one per route. Recorded bucket-scope = shared (D19). The d02m-fresh4 draft and the d02m-fresh5 draft word the question and the option differently; the answer is unchanged (shared).

D17 window-boundary (exclusive): a request exactly at 60 s starts a new window, so the window is fixed, not sliding. The window items anchor on the first match with duration 60000 ms and boundary exclusive; probe s17 is at 60000 ms. The d02m-fresh4 draft words the question and the option differently; the answer is unchanged.

choice_rules.option_label_match: (?i)^Only limit signed-in users, leave anonymous unchanged$
choice_rules.reason: q-anon: no. The order says each signed-in user (orders.json, the rate-limit sentence), so anonymous requests are not limited. The link API already answers anonymous callers 401. Option: auth-only.

scope_edits.reason: The drafted item (limit-get-links) names no probe step. The over-limit GET /api/links is anchored on probe step s14 of login-over-quota by i-quota-get-links, which is kept.

The drafted item covers every POST /api/links at any step. The same rule is anchored on the corpus steps that send the 11th request, a relogin, a request inside the window, and bob's own quota (i-quota-window, i-quota-relogin, i-quota-inside-window, mk-bob-quota). Boundary is exclusive: a request at 60 s starts a new window.

No probe sends more than ten DELETE requests, so this item cannot be judged; a DELETE status change stays out of scope and is reported. Coordinator decision 4: DELETE /api/links/:code is accepted as is and is named in the window items' text. The d02m-fresh4 draft names this item limit-delete-link; the decision is the same. (drafted id in d02m-fresh5 is limit-delete-links)

Standing rule 2 (D10): the d02m-fresh4 draft must-keep signup-keep names step signup-check, which is not a corpus step. Re-anchored on the first corpus step with method POST, route /api/signup and principal kind any: probe signup-store, step s1, equals_base on status. The corpus also has an s1 in signup-rules; the server validates the id at revise_scope.

Earlier decision D9 (keep-login): the d02m-fresh4 draft has no login must-keep, so it is added, as keep-redirect was. Re-anchored on login-over-quota s11 (POST /api/login after the link quota is used), equals_base on status.

Earlier coordinator decision: redirect keep anchored on probe step s3 (GET /${link_code}, route /:code, anonymous, status equals base). The d02t foreman draft has no redirect must-keep, so the rule is added, not replaced. In d02m-fresh5 the draft already has keep-redirect; it is replaced with the same anchor (s3), not added.
